compass.lensDefMarket: All jobs matching enabled discovery probes — the broad market scan.
compass.lensDefFocus: Only jobs matching your personal focus intents.
compass.lensDefCompare: Side-by-side market vs focus counts (needs at least one focus intent).
compass.lensDefRising: Skills with positive growth in the period (recent half vs previous).
compass.lensDefCooling: Skills with flat or negative growth in the period.
compass.lensDefGeo: Breakdown by country code from observed jobs.
compass.compareUnavailable: Compare needs paired market and focus series. Save a focus intent or wait for the next crawl.
compass.crawlEmpty: No observed jobs yet — run Sources or wait for the next crawl.
compass.thinMarketWarn: Thin market sample (n={n}). Enable more discovery probes or wait for the next crawl.

research.marketScanSubtitle: Discovery probes shape the market lens. Enable a few broad topics — they are not personal focus.
research.focusSubtitle: Personal stacks for Focus / Compare lenses. Kept separate from the market narrative.
research.apiNotReadyBody: The research intents endpoint is not available yet (404). Start the backend with research routes enabled, then retry.
research.discoveryWarn: Only {count} discovery probe(s) enabled. Soft minimum is {min} for a healthier market scan.
research.emptyDiscovery: No discovery intents yet. Seed the watchlist or wait for backend defaults.
research.probeSearchJobsHint: To search job records already in the database, open
research.probeFilterEmptyHint: Clear the filter or try a different keyword.
research.emptyFocus: No focus intents yet. Add one below — free text for search-mode collectors.
research.createFocusHint: Describe what you want collectors to search for. Included in the next daily sync when enabled.
research.countriesHint: Declared geo for this focus — used only as a Country filter suggestion, never auto-applied.
research.suggestCountries: Focus intents declare {codes}. Apply them to the Country filter?

charts.guideTechGraph: Technologies linked when they co-appear in the same observed job ad.
charts.guideTechGraphRead: Node size reflects total co-mention weight. Edge thickness is support (joint ads). Click a node to focus that technology. Show caps how many nodes appear. Association only — not causation.
charts.defTechGraphEdge: Two skills mentioned in the same stored job.
charts.defTechGraphSupport: Count of jobs that mention both technologies together.
charts.empty: No chart data for this period.
charts.topNAriaRiseCool: Total bars: half rising, half cooling when both sides exist
charts.riseCoolNoCooling: Show {n} = up to {rise} rising + {cool} cooling. This period has no cooling skills (all ok grew) — showing {shown} rising.
charts.riseCoolNoRising: Show {n} = up to {rise} rising + {cool} cooling. This period has no rising skills — showing {shown} cooling.
charts.riseCoolBalanceNote: Show {n} reserves {rise} rising + {cool} cooling. Available with enough sample: {shownRise} rising, {shownCool} cooling.
charts.defRise: Skills whose mention count grew in the recent half of the period vs the earlier half.
charts.defCool: Skills whose mention count fell (or did not grow) over the same comparison.
charts.defGrowth: Percent change recent vs previous mentions. Needs enough sample on both sides.
charts.defMarket: Volume from the broad market lens (discovery probes), not your personal focus.
charts.defFocus: Volume limited to jobs matching your saved focus intents.
charts.defN: Period sample size (all ok skills) — stable when you change Show.
charts.defThin: Too few observations for strong conclusions — treat the shape as directional only.
charts.defCountry: ISO country code from the job record when known.
charts.defJobs: Count of observed (stored) job ads in that country for the period.
charts.defMixKey: Classified field value (remote type, contract type, …). Unknown means missing.
charts.defRankLabel: Technology, language code, or source name ranked by observed count.
charts.defMedian: Median advertised rate in the unit/currency bucket (observed text only).
charts.defIqr: Interquartile range of advertised rates when sample size allows.
charts.guideRiseCool: Technologies ranked by mention growth (rising) vs decline (cooling) over the period halves. Show N splits evenly (N/2 each side).
charts.guideRiseCoolRead: Bars to the right of zero grew; to the left cooled. Show 10 → 5+5, Show 30 → 15+15 — empty sides are not filled from the other. Thin samples are flagged. Toggle table for exact counts.
charts.guideRankBars: Ranked counts for the selected dimension (language, source, …) in the current lens.
charts.guideRankBarsRead: Longer bars = higher observed count. Use Show to change how many rows appear; table view sorts and filters the same values.
charts.guideRatesBox: Median advertised rates by currency/unit bucket from extracted pay text.
charts.guideRatesBoxRead: Compare within the same unit only. Whiskers (when shown) are the interquartile spread; small n means treat as directional.
charts.guideCompareDual: Side-by-side mention volumes for Market vs Focus on the same technologies.
charts.guideCompareDualRead: Each pair of bars is one skill. Large Market with small Focus means the skill is common broadly but rare in your intents.
charts.guideWorldMap: Geographic density of observed jobs by country (unknown country excluded from the map).
charts.guideWorldMapRead: Darker countries have more stored ads in the period. This is database coverage, not a census of national labour markets.
charts.guideMultiSeries: Time series of top series lines (technologies, countries, or rate medians) over the selected window.
charts.guideMultiSeriesRead: Each coloured line is one series. Rising paths mean more volume over time in stored data. Switch to table to sort and filter exact points.
charts.guideHeatDefault: Two-dimensional matrix of co-occurrence or joint counts in observed ads.
charts.guideHeatDefaultRead: Darker cells mean higher joint counts. Read axes labels for what rows and columns mean; pale cells are thin or zero.
charts.guideDonutMix: Share of jobs by a categorical field (remote type, contract type, source mix, …).
charts.guideDonutMixRead: Slice size is the share of the sample. Unknown means missing classification. Table view lists counts and percentages.
charts.guideSparkline: Jobs-per-day (or per bucket) volume over the selected period.
charts.guideSparklineRead: Peaks may reflect crawls or posting bursts in stored data. Table lists each day and count for exact values.

common.noteThinEvidence: {thin_n} jobs ({pct}%) are thin evidence (title/snippet/synthetic) and are excluded from skills/rates/briefs when min_evidence=standard.
common.noteCappedSources: Slice includes capped or snapshot sources ({sources}) — counts are not a census of the national market.

applications.title: Applications & Outcomes
applications.subtitle: Personal pipeline metrics — not market metrics.
applications.tableRepresents: Your personal application log — dates, channels, responses, and outcomes you recorded. Not market demand.
applications.tableHowToRead: Sort any column; filter with the search box. Newest applications appear first by default. Empty cells mean you have not filled that field yet.

profile.title: Profile & Skills
profile.gapsEmpty: No skill gaps in the current window.
profile.localStorageHint: Your profile stays in this browser (localStorage). Market gaps use observed job demand only.
profile.skillsHint: Add a skill, then press Enter or Add.
profile.certsHint: Optional. Add one certification at a time.

stackCompass.title: Stack Compass
stackCompass.subtitle: Complementary skills observed with your stack — not vanity top-N trends.
stackCompass.trendsOnlyHidden: Stack Compass coaching is hidden in Trends-only mode. Switch to Guided to see learning candidates.
stackCompass.needSkills: Add at least 3 skills in your profile for stronger adjacent recommendations.
stackCompass.rateThin: Rate check: insufficient advertised samples for this skill.
stackCompass.notVanity: Scores penalize commodity skills (high frequency + low lift). Observed ads only — not earnings or hire guarantees.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.subtitle: Rules show evidence that triggered them.
alerts.empty: No alerts yet. Evaluate rules to surface evidence.

report.title: Weekly report
report.subtitle: Built from structured backend KPIs. LLM narrative only if provider healthy; otherwise deterministic Markdown.

eurostat.title: Eurostat context (reference)
eurostat.subtitle: Official EU statistics for orientation only — not observed freelance rates from job postings.

taxonomy.title: Taxonomy reference lookup
taxonomy.subtitle: Free public taxonomies (ESCO EU, JobTech Sweden). Labels only — not observed demand or rates.

prefs.title: Dashboard preferences
prefs.localeHint: Saved with your preferences and restored on refresh.

trends.title: Technology Trends
trends.subtitleGuided: Last {days} days · Half-period comparison of observed skill mentions. Growth is marked insufficient_data when previous window sample is zero or support is below threshold.
trends.hintTechnology: Canonical skill or tool name extracted from job text.
trends.hintCategory: Taxonomy bucket for the technology (e.g. language, framework).
trends.hintRecent: How many times this skill was mentioned in the more recent half of the period.
trends.hintPrevious: Mentions in the earlier half of the same period (baseline for growth).
trends.hintGrowth: Percent change of recent vs previous mentions. Positive = rising demand in ads; negative = cooling. Needs enough sample on both sides.
trends.hintStatus: ok = growth is computable; insufficient_data = too few mentions to trust the %.
trends.hintMarket: Mention volume in the broad market lens (discovery probes).
trends.hintFocus: Mention volume limited to your saved focus intents.
trends.compareEmpty: Compare needs paired market and focus series with at least two technologies. Save a focus intent or wait for the next crawl.
trends.emptyTable: No technology rows for this lens and period.
trends.tableRepresents: Skill mention volume in the recent vs previous half of the selected period, with growth % where sample allows.
trends.tableHowToRead: Positive growth % = rising mentions in ads; negative = cooling. Status insufficient_data means the % is not trustworthy. Sort columns or filter by technology name. In Compare, Market and Focus are side-by-side volumes for the same skill.

countries.title: Country Comparison
countries.subtitle: Last {days} days · observed jobs by country_code in this DB
countries.legalNote: Not legal/tax advice. Remote ≠ Italian-resident access.
countries.hintJobsObserved: Count of stored job ads attributed to this country in the period.
countries.hintRemoteShare: Share of those ads marked remote (or hybrid) in our classification.
countries.hintB2bShare: Share classified as freelance / B2B / contractor-style contracts.
countries.hintResidence: Ads that explicitly allow or restrict work from a stated residence — rare, text-derived.
countries.hintTopTech: Most frequent skills mentioned in jobs for this country (observed only).
countries.empty: No country breakdown for this lens yet.
countries.tableRepresents: Observed job counts and remote/B2B shares by ISO country in this database for the active lens and period.
countries.tableHowToRead: Jobs observed is the row weight — sort by it to find densest countries. Remote and B2B shares are percentages of those jobs. Top tech lists frequent skills in that country. Filter by ISO code or skill name; the map above uses the same corpus.

languages.title: Language requirements
languages.subtitle: Last {days} days · human languages extracted from ad text (not programming languages).
languages.compareCounts: Compare · market n={market} · focus n={focus} · overlap={overlap}
languages.hintLanguage: ISO 639-1 code extracted from the posting (en, it, de, …).
languages.hintJobs: Canonical open jobs whose language_requirements list includes this code.
languages.hintShare: Share of the filtered sample that mentions this language (a job may count in several).
languages.hintCoverage: Share of jobs with at least one detected human-language requirement.
languages.empty: No language extractions for this lens yet.
languages.tableRepresents: Human languages (not programming languages) extracted from job text, with job counts and share of the filtered sample.
languages.tableHowToRead: Jobs is how many ads mention that language; Share is relative to the sample (a job can count in several languages). Coverage in the header is the share of ads with at least one language. Sort or filter by language code.

certificationsPage.title: Certification demand benchmarks
certificationsPage.subtitle: External published rankings (surveys and job-ad studies) plus observed mentions in this FMI corpus. Not a global market-size estimate.
certificationsPage.corpusEmpty: No certification mentions extracted in this lens yet.
certificationsPage.skillsoftCaption: Survey: certifications IT professionals planned to pursue (count of respondents). Source: IT Skills & Salary Report 2024–2025.
certificationsPage.adzunaTitle: Named in US job ads by role (Adzuna via CertWorthIT)
certificationsPage.adzunaCaption: Share of role ads that name the certification (US, Oct 2026 snapshot). Each row is relative to its own role — not cross-role volume.
certificationsPage.pearsonCaption: Share of exam candidates planning certifications in each specialty (Value of Certification Report 2025).
certificationsPage.disclaimer: External charts are curated snapshots with attribution. Methodology differs from FMI evidence-first counts. Prefer the corpus chart for what appears in ads you stored.
certificationsPage.byCountryCaption: Choropleth = open ads with ≥1 extracted certification. Select a country for its local top certifications (observed mentions).
certificationsPage.byCountryTableCaption: Countries ranked by ads with certifications
certificationsPage.byCountryEmpty: No country-level certification mentions in this lens yet.
certificationsPage.byCountryLoadFailed: Could not load certifications by country.

rates.title: Rate Explorer
rates.subtitle: Last {days} days · advertised rates observed in DB only — never invented or scraped from paywalls.
rates.compareCounts: Compare · market n={market} · focus n={focus} · overlap={overlap}
rates.hintCountry: ISO country code of the job (or unknown when the ad did not state one).
rates.hintCurrency: Currency as written in the ad (EUR, USD, CHF, …).
rates.hintUnit: Pay period in the ad: hour, day, month, or project — compare only within the same unit.
rates.hintN: Sample size: how many jobs with a rate fall in this country/currency/unit bucket.
rates.hintMedian: Middle advertised rate when sorted — half the sample is at or below this value.
rates.hintP25: 25th percentile: 25% of rates in this bucket are at or below this value (lower end of the spread).
rates.hintP75: 75th percentile: 75% of rates are at or below this value (upper end of the typical spread).
rates.hintStatus: ok = enough sample to show stats; insufficient_data = too few rates for reliable percentiles.
rates.empty: No rate rows for this lens yet.
rates.tableRepresents: Advertised pay percentiles grouped by country, currency, and pay unit — only rates found in stored job text.
rates.tableHowToRead: Compare only within the same unit (hour/day/month). n is sample size; median is the middle rate; P25–P75 is the typical spread. Status insufficient_data means too few rates. Filter by country or currency; rates are never invented.

skills.title: Skill co-occurrence
skills.subtitle: Pairs of technologies that appear together in the same observed job. This shows association in ads you stored — not that one skill causes the other.
skills.compareCounts: Compare · market n={market} · focus n={focus} · overlap={overlap}
skills.hintTechA: First technology in the pair (order is alphabetical by id, not importance).
skills.hintTechB: Second technology in the same job as Tech A.
skills.hintSupport: How many jobs mention both technologies together in this period.
skills.hintLift: How often they co-occur vs chance if independent. Above 1 = stronger-than-random pairing; below 1 = rarer together. Not causation.
skills.hintJaccard: Overlap score from 0 to 1: jobs with both ÷ jobs with either. Higher means they share more of the same ads.
skills.empty: No pairs yet for this lens — run collectors or import jobs first.
skills.tableRepresents: Technology pairs that appear together in the same observed job ad, with support count and association scores.
skills.tableHowToRead: Support is co-mention count. Lift > 1 means they co-occur more than chance; Jaccard is overlap 0–1. High support with lift near 1 is common pairing, not causation. Sort by support or lift; filter by technology name.

relations.title: Relations
relations.subtitle: Last {days} days · observed co-occurrence, tech×country matrix, and temporal series.
relations.subtitleGuided: Last {days} days · correlative views under one period, lens, and country filter. Association in stored ads — not market size or causation.
relations.methodologyNote: Co-occurrence shows technologies that appear together in the same observed job. That is association in ads you stored — not that one skill causes another, and not a census of the external market.
relations.graphEmptySeed: No co-occurrence neighbors for this technology above min support.
relations.graphPickHint: Pick a technology to see what else appears in the same ads, or explore the overview graph.
relations.emptyHeat: No matrix cells for this lens and period.
relations.emptySeries: No series points for this lens and period.
relations.guideHeatTechTech: Co-occurrence of technologies in the same ad. Darker cells = more joint mentions (support).
relations.guideHeatTechTechRead: Symmetrical matrix: cell (A,B) matches (B,A). Scan dark bands for frequent stacks. Association in stored ads only — not causation or market size.
relations.guideHeatTechCountry: How often each technology appears in jobs attributed to each country.
relations.guideHeatTechCountryRead: Rows are countries, columns technologies (or vice versa per axes). Darker = more jobs. Thin rows mean sparse geo coverage for that skill.
relations.guideHeatLangCountry: Human-language requirements crossed with job country codes.
relations.guideHeatLangCountryRead: Dark cells mean many ads in that country mention that language. Useful for language demand by market — not programming languages.
relations.guideHeatRoleTech: Role-family labels crossed with technologies mentioned in the same ads.
relations.guideHeatRoleTechRead: Find which skills cluster with which role families. Empty bands mean few classified roles for that skill in this corpus.
relations.guideHeatSeniorityTech: Seniority bands crossed with technologies in the same ads.
relations.guideHeatSeniorityTechRead: Darker cells = more co-mentions. Compare junior vs senior stacks for the same tech; thin samples stay pale.
relations.guideSeriesTech: Daily (or bucketed) mention counts for top technologies over the period.
relations.guideSeriesTechRead: Each line is a technology. Rising lines = more mentions over time in stored ads. Toggle table view to sort/filter exact values.
relations.guideSeriesCountry: Job counts over time for top countries in the corpus.
relations.guideSeriesCountryRead: Each line is a country ISO code. Spikes may reflect crawls, not real market shocks. Use the table toggle for exact numbers.
relations.guideSeriesRates: Median advertised rates over time for top currency/unit buckets.
relations.guideSeriesRatesRead: Compare only within the same unit. Medians need enough n; flat or missing segments mean thin rate coverage.

quality.title: Data Quality
quality.subtitle: Quality describes this database coverage, not the external market.
quality.compareCounts: Compare · market n={market} · focus n={focus} · overlap={overlap}
quality.catalogUnsupportedHint: Unsupported usually means reference/stats, agency sites without a public API, or demoted duplicate stubs — not broken crawlers. Switch the filter to inspect them.
quality.hintSource: Job board or feed key that supplied the ads.
quality.hintConnector: Collector implementation wired to that source.
quality.hintN: How many canonical jobs from this source are in the current lens/period.
quality.hintPctKnownCountry: Share of those jobs with a real ISO country (not unknown).
quality.hintPctThin: Share tagged thin evidence (capped/snapshot). High means weaker coverage.
quality.hintPctRate: Share that include at least one extracted pay figure.
quality.hintLastSeen: When we last ingested a job from this source.
quality.hintStatus: Collector health for the source (ok / attention / errors).
quality.hintEnabled: Whether the source is turned on for crawls.
quality.hintLastSuccess: Timestamp of the last successful collection run.
quality.hintNotes: Ops notes or limits recorded for this source.
quality.metric_pct_with_valid_date_label: Jobs with a valid publish date
quality.metric_pct_with_valid_date_hint: Share of canonical jobs that have a usable published_at (needed for trends and “jobs/day”).
quality.metric_pct_known_country_hint: Share with a real ISO country (not “unknown”). Low values weaken geo charts and country filters.
quality.metric_pct_known_contract_label: Jobs with a known contract type
quality.metric_pct_known_contract_hint: Share classified as freelance / B2B / employment / etc. (not “unknown”).
quality.metric_pct_with_rate_hint: Share that include at least one extracted pay/rate figure. Rates are never invented.
quality.metric_pct_thin_hint: Share marked as thin evidence (capped/snapshot sources). High is worse — excluded from skills/rates when min_evidence=standard.
quality.metric_thin_n_hint: Absolute number of canonical jobs tagged thin evidence in this lens/filter.
quality.metric_duplicate_non_canonical_hint: Rows kept as non-canonical duplicates of another job. Zero means dedup is clean.
quality.bySourceRepresents: Per-source coverage quality: job counts and shares with known country, thin evidence, and extracted rates.
quality.bySourceHowToRead: n is jobs from that source in the lens. High % thin is weaker evidence; high % with rate helps pay charts. Sort by n or quality %; filter by source name.
quality.catalogRepresents: Connector catalog status — enabled flag, last success, and ops notes for each registered source.
quality.catalogHowToRead: Use the status filter to hide unsupported stubs, then text-search by name. Enabled=on means the crawler may run it. Last success empty means never collected successfully.

jobs.title: Job Explorer
jobs.subtitle: DB-only list for the active demand lens. Filters do not crawl sources.
jobs.empty: No matching jobs for this lens yet.
jobs.emptyHint: Enable discovery probes or save a focus intent, then wait for the next crawl:
jobs.loadFailedHint: Check that the API is up and API_CORS_ORIGINS includes this UI origin (localhost and 127.0.0.1 are different).
jobs.evidenceThinHint: Thin evidence (capped/snapshot source) — excluded from skills/rates when min_evidence=standard
jobs.tableRepresents: Canonical jobs stored in this database for the active lens and filters — titles, companies, geo, contract, and tech tags.
jobs.tableHowToRead: Use the filter form above to narrow the corpus, then sort by published date, title, company, country, contract, or source. Thin badges mark weaker evidence. Open URL to see the original ad.

explorer.title: Explore
explorer.subtitle: Search job records already in Postgres. Filters query the database only — they do not crawl sources.
explorer.loadFailedHint: Check that the API is running, then submit the search again.
explorer.empty: No matching jobs in the database yet.
explorer.emptyHint: Wait for the daily crawler, or refresh a selected intent from sources. Manage probes and focus here:
explorer.refreshHint: Syncs one discovery or focus intent from external sources. Daily crawlers remain the primary pipeline.
explorer.refreshNeedsIntent: No research intents yet — create one first:
explorer.refreshOk: Sync finished — list refreshed from the database.

sources.title: Sources & LLM Control
sources.subtitle: Only authorized/public connectors are runnable. Prefer free public APIs/RSS over paid aggregator scaffolds. Catalog statuses come from verified probes — never invent access.
sources.activeNeedRun: {count} of {total} ACTIVE sources have no insert evidence — Run them to prove ingest.
sources.activeAllHaveInserts: All {total} ACTIVE sources have CollectionRun insert evidence.
sources.emptyRunnableFilterBody: Switch to All or enable more sources. Credentialed scaffolds need env keys before they can prove ACTIVE.
sources.kindFreeHint: Public API or RSS — no paid aggregator keys required
sources.kindCredHint: Paid or partner API — set env keys, then Run to prove ingest
sources.filterKindAria: Filter runnable connectors by access type
sources.partnerBoardsNote: Indeed, LinkedIn, and similar boards need official partner/publisher API access. They appear under Access → Needs credentials (or Status → NEEDS_CREDENTIALS), not under Free or Runnable, until a connector and keys exist. Scraping is out of scope.
sources.catalogOnlyHint: catalog ACTIVE, not seeded in DB
sources.emptyRunnableBody: Seed the catalog or enable a source with connector_status=enabled to run collections here.
sources.emptyCatalog: No catalog entries match these filters.
sources.statusNeedsCredsHint: Set env credentials, then Run to prove ingest
sources.runFreeDone: Done: {ok} ok, {failed} failed, inserted={inserted} (free public only; skipped paid scaffolds).
sources.freeActiveSubtitle: Public connectors marked ACTIVE (no paid API keys). Last run from CollectionRun / last_success_at.
sources.freeActiveEmpty: No free ACTIVE connectors in catalog/DB.
sources.credSubtitle: Secrets in encrypted DB (preferred) or env fallback. Credentials set ≠ ACTIVE — ACTIVE still needs a live ingest. See docs/ops/RUNBOOKS.md (connectors)
sources.credKeysSetHint: Keys present (DB or env). Catalog ACTIVE still requires a successful live run.
sources.credOpsTokenHint: Break-glass when not signed in as Keycloak admin. Tab-only (sessionStorage).
sources.credAdminRequired: Connector credentials require a Keycloak admin role (or ops break-glass token).
sources.credAdminJwtHint: Using your admin session — no ops token needed.
sources.credOpsTokenNeeded: Enter the ops token to load fields.
sources.credDeleteConfirm: Remove encrypted DB credentials for this connector? Env fallback will apply if set.

assistant.title: Prompt → dashboard / report
assistant.subtitle: Uses the same propose/validate path as MCP analytics. Specs are grounded in observed metrics — rates are never invented. Current prefs: {viewMode}, {days}d.
assistant.promptPlaceholder: e.g. Show demand trends for the last 90 days, trends-only
assistant.compassSubtitle: Pick a question. Answers use counts from jobs already stored here — we do not invent market size.
assistant.noCandidates: No watch candidates in this brief.
assistant.briefPurpose_rising_cooling: Which skills show up more (or less) often in ads versus the previous half of the window.
assistant.briefPurpose_where_demand: Which countries have more observed ads, and how remote they are.
assistant.briefPurpose_adjacent: Skills that often sit next to yours in ads, but are not in your profile yet.
assistant.briefPurpose_focus_vs_market: How many ads the broad market covers versus your personal focus.
assistant.briefPurpose_suggest_watches: Topic ideas to follow (watches). Nothing is saved until you accept one.
assistant.briefLimits_rising_cooling: We only count technology mentions in stored ads. A large % change is not proof the whole market grew — probes or sources can move. Missing rates stay empty, not zero.
assistant.briefLimits_where_demand: Countries come from the country field on observed ads, not an official census. Not legal or tax advice.
assistant.briefLimits_adjacent: “Adjacent” means co-mentioned in the same ads as your skills — not causation or a job guarantee.
assistant.briefLimits_focus_vs_market: Compare uses ads linked to market probes and your focus intents. Overlap counts in both. This is not total market size.
assistant.briefLimits_suggest_watches: Suggestions only. Nothing is written to the database until you click Accept on a watch.
assistant.noWatchCandidates: No watch candidates in this brief.
assistant.reportPdfFailed: Could not build the PDF report

llmAdmin.title: LLM runtime (admin)
llmAdmin.subtitle: Configure Ollama, OpenAI-compatible, or Gemini. API keys are never shown after save.
llmAdmin.needAdmin: Sign in as admin or enter OPS token to edit.

studyAdvisor.title: Study Advisor
studyAdvisor.subtitle: A study plan grounded in Stack Compass, with a week calendar that skips busy hours and spreads study for work–life balance.
studyAdvisor.trendsOnlyHidden: Study Advisor is hidden in Trends-only mode. Switch to Guided.
studyAdvisor.needSkills: Add at least 3 skills in Profile for a fuller plan (thin profiles get a coverage stub).
studyAdvisor.stackHint: Grounded in skills that appear in the job ads we already collected.
studyAdvisor.emptyStack: No clear skill targets yet — add profile skills or widen the market window.
studyAdvisor.milestonesHint: Rough waypoints — adjust after each week if your calendar changes.
studyAdvisor.milestonesEmpty: No checkpoints yet — generate a plan first.
studyAdvisor.refineSkipped: Live adjustment unavailable right now — try again later.
studyAdvisor.busyHint: Mark when you are unavailable — several blocks per day are fine. Study is spread across the week into free preferred windows (work–life balance).
studyAdvisor.calHint: Paste a private ICS link from Google Calendar, Aruba, Outlook, or Apple. We mark calls and events as busy for this week, then you can replan study around them.
studyAdvisor.calHowTo: Google: Calendar settings → Integrate calendar → Secret address in iCal format. Aruba / Outlook: look for “publish” or “ICS subscribe” URL.
studyAdvisor.calSyncOk: Imported {imported} busy blocks from {events} events (week of {week}).
studyAdvisor.calSyncFail: Could not read that calendar feed.
studyAdvisor.calendarWlbHint: Study is distributed across days to avoid overload.
studyAdvisor.limitCorpus: Suggestions come only from skills seen in real job ads — not a promise that studying them will pay off.
studyAdvisor.limitGapOnly: Some targets are demand gaps with few co-mentions next to your current skills.
studyAdvisor.limitScores: Numbers are mention counts in our corpus, not market size or salary.
studyAdvisor.limitNoWindow: No free study window left after busy hours — free an evening/weekend or lower weekly hours.
studyAdvisor.limitPartial: Only {gotH}h {gotM}m fit around busy hours (target {wantH}h/week). Free evenings/weekends or lower hours.
studyAdvisor.limitWlb: Study spread across {days} days for work–life balance.
studyAdvisor.limitDropped: We dropped a few suggested topics that were not backed by the job-ad evidence.
studyAdvisor.limitLlmFallback: The language model was unavailable; this is the rule-based plan instead.
studyAdvisor.limitThin: Thin data this week — the plan is a cautious stub from what we could observe.
studyAdvisor.limitNoCandidates: No learning candidates matched your profile in the current window.
